prospect.name: Hamdi Hmimy
prospect.location: Dallas, Texas, USA — relocating within the next two weeks
prospect.occupation: Technology sales — 'I sell technology'; had just closed a good quarter and was held back to present internally
prospect.family_status: Recently married. No children currently; refers to playing with kids as a future goal.
prospect.training_background: Long-term bodybuilder. Reached 7-8% body fat about six months ago, describing it as the leanest he has been, using traditional splits, cutting and 1,700-1,800 calories. Had a bodybuilding trainer for about eighteen months, and separate coaching for calisthenics and basketball. Plays basketball regularly. Did the carnivore diet for a period. Has been doing kettlebell work on his own for the past week or two and enjoys it. Says he has gained about eight pounds of water and fat in the last two months through travel and now has 'no structure'. Currently self-assesses at 12-13% body fat.
prospect.medical: Self-described 'really bad shoulders'. Reports hip tightness from bodybuilding and from sitting all day, that 'everything started creaking' since turning 30, and that he now has to stretch far more than usual. No diagnosis, treatment, clinician or history was given, because none was asked for — the rep put no health, injury or limitation question at any point in the call.

signals: Self-directed and demonstrably capable — his own method already produced the result he is trying to return to: 'I know how to get shredded', 'I can get there pretty quickly if I just do the bodybuilding stuff, cutting, eating 1,800, 1,700 calories'
Explicit self-sufficiency caveat when scoring the offer: 'there's always a part of me that's like I could do this myself, it'll just take longer'
Counter-anchored on price with a specific number rather than objecting in general terms: 'I wanted to see more $2,000 to $2,500 for three months'
Bought down to the $200/mo tier the moment he understood it contained the one component he wanted

OVERLAP NOTE: on profile alone he reads as the_optimizer — fit, successful, and framed by the rep as going from a 10 to a 12 out of 10, which he accepted. He is assigned here instead because the defining clause of the_optimizer, that price is a quality signal rather than a barrier, is directly contradicted three times on this call.

goals.text: Get his physique back after gaining about eight pounds in two months, returning toward 7-8% body fat
Keep the muscle he has while training a different way
Become functional and athletic again — loosen tight hips, regain explosiveness, stop losing athleticism on the basketball court
Get cardiovascular work into a session he actually enjoys rather than doing cardio separately
Learn kettlebells properly and safely as a new sport, with correct form from a professional
Wake up with energy again — 'I just love waking up with energy... the last couple of weeks I wake up and I'm like, I don't want to do anything'
Stay able to play sports, play with his future kids, and do athletic things outdoors with his wife
Stop feeling like he is losing his youth and his functional self at 30
Shift lifestyle away from heavy-carb bodybuilding toward cleaner, more ancestral eating

pains.text: Bodybuilding left him tight and non-functional — 'my hips were super tight. Everything was really tight... I just didn't feel functional. Looked good. Felt bad.'
Lost structure entirely over the last two months through travel and an imminent house move — 'Right now, I have no structure in the last two months'
Turning 30 and noticing decline — 'Everything started creaking. I have to stretch way more than usual'
Bad shoulders, disclosed while explaining why form matters to him
Sits all day and can feel his hips tightening as a result
Body dysmorphia by his own naming — 'I'm probably at 12-13%, but I feel bad'
Bored of isolation-based training and unwilling to bolt mobility on as a separate routine — 'it's a whole other routine you have to do... it's not intertwined with the bodybuilding workout splits'
Motivation has dipped with the weight gain — 'My body weight is correlated with my performance in the real world... I've slipped a little bit'
Does not know how to handle a kettlebell safely — 'I just don't know how to safely throw a kettlebell around'

objections.raw_quote: The $4,000 is a little bit more than I was expecting. I wanted to see more $2,000 to $2,500 for three months.
objections.rep_response: Restated the six and twelve month prices, then offered financing across 12 or 24 months through partner lenders

objections.raw_quote: Almost $1,300 a month is a bit high for me.
objections.rep_response: Pointed out the twelve-month tier works out around $800/mo and repeated the financing option

objections.raw_quote: Is that interest-free or no? ... That's tough. This is out of what I was expecting.
objections.rep_response: Confirmed there is 'a little bit of interest on each' without giving a rate, and on the next turn disqualified the prospect from the coaching offer entirely

objections.raw_quote: there's always a part of me that's like I could do this myself, it'll just take longer right
objections.rep_response: No challenge. The rep did not run the information-isn't-the-problem move and went to price

objections.raw_quote: the biggest thing I care about is form. But like the nutrition, like I know how to get shredded. I just don't know how to safely throw a kettlebell around.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the reduced scope and recommended the $200/mo self-paced product instead of the bundle

offer.payment_plan_terms: Any tier can be spread over 12 months via Paver, or up to 24 months via the lender the rep called 'Plano', subject to a decent credit score. Interest was confirmed to exist — 'A little bit of interest on each' — but no rate, no total and no schedule was given, and no plan was actually built.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: On the $1,200 one-month tier: 'we call it love it or leave it', with the differential credited toward a longer tier afterwards — 'Instead of paying four grand, you pay $2,800'. On Primal University: 'you can cancel it at any time. So some people come in for three months, they get what they need, and then they're off.'

evidence: The rep disqualified the prospect from the core offer himself: 'To be honest with you, Hamdi, just based on what I hear, I don't think you need one-on-one coaching, at least for now, brother... If you want to learn kettlebells, probably the best thing for you is Primal University.'
Price was rejected three separate times, with a specific counter-anchor of $2,000-2,500 against a $4,000 three-month tier
Prospect accepted the redirect: 'Okay, cool. Yeah, I think I'm going to go with that for now.'

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: this is not a clean loss for the company. The prospect was sent a Primal University link, logged in during the call and said 'I'll look a little bit more into this, and I think that's the route I'll probably be taking' — so a $200/mo subscription may well follow, off this recording.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: no payment of any kind was taken on the call. The rep offered to complete it live — 'it's best to do in this moment so I can just check that you'll get onboarded correctly' — and the prospect deferred because he was on his computer without his details set up.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to create a Skool account and review Primal University in his own time; he has the rep's personal WhatsApp and said he would text once logged in

notable.note: The clearest clinical finding in the batch. The prospect volunteered 'I have really bad shoulders' at 00:03:33 while explaining why the overhead around-the-world movements caught his eye, and said plainly at 00:26:52 that 'I just don't know how to safely throw a kettlebell around'. Not one health or injury question was asked, and the rep then steered him to Primal University — the self-paced video product with no form review and no coach feedback loop — despite the prospect having just named safe form as the single thing he was buying. The commercial judgement was honest and probably correct; the safety consequence of the routing was the opposite of what the disclosure called for. Separately, the rep told this prospect there are 30 one-to-one clients, having told a prospect the previous day there are about 60.

quality.notes: Persistent short-turn inversion, and one long block at 00:20:00 to 00:21:00 where a full prospect answer and the rep's next-steps transition are merged under a single Hamdi Hmimy label. Clear individual examples: 'Congratulations, by the way' at 00:03:23 is labelled Hamdi but is the rep responding to the marriage; 'I sell technology' at 00:17:43 is labelled Hamdi correctly but the question preceding it is split across labels; 'How do you feel, brother, about everything I've gone over?' at 00:19:23 is labelled Hamdi and is the rep. The rep also calls the prospect 'Andy' once at 00:13:31 and initially guessed 'Hamid'. Roles resolved from content throughout.
